post.description: Register a new account; duplicate emails yield a 409 CONFLICT envelope.
Verifies credentials server-side and issues the access JWT and the opaque refresh credential as HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict cookies (Chapter 2, Section 9). No token material in the body.

post.summary: Exchange a Firebase ID token for SentinelGPT session cookies
post.description: Verifies a Firebase ID token server-side (signature, audience, issuer, expiry against Google's public JWKs) and resolves or provisions the canonical SentinelGPT account for that identity (ADR-0010), then issues the same HttpOnly session cookies as POST /auth/login. The client never sends a user ID — identity comes exclusively from the verified token. Requires FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID to be configured (503 otherwise).

get.summary: Return the authenticated user (session restore probe)
get.description: Cheap identity probe used by the SPA on page load to restore the in-memory user from the still-attached HttpOnly access cookie. Returns 200 with the same UserInfo the login response uses; returns the standard 401 UNAUTHENTICATED envelope when no valid session is attached. No token material is ever returned in the body.

post.summary: Rotate the refresh credential and reissue both cookies
post.description: Reads the HttpOnly refreshToken cookie (requires X-Refresh-Request: 1). Every call rotates both cookies. Presenting a rotated-out credential revokes the entire token family and returns 401 (Ch5 §2 reuse detection).

parameters.name: x-refresh-request
parameters.description: CSRF mitigation per SRS Ch2 §9. Same-origin JS sets this custom header; cross-site form posts cannot. Must be the literal string '1'.

post.summary: Revoke the presented refresh session and clear cookies
post.description: Requires X-Refresh-Request: 1. Revokes the presented ACTIVE refresh credential server-side (idempotent) and clears both auth cookies.

get.summary: Per-finding AI explanation (validated or fallback template)
get.description:
Return the AI explanation for one finding.

The endpoint is honest about provenance: a finding without an
explanation is served a deterministic fallback template (NEVER a 404
or an empty body) so the user always gets a readable explanation.
The ``validationStatus`` field of the response is the single
boolean the UI needs to label the answer correctly.

get.summary: Render the canonical report for one scan in the requested format
get.description:
Render the report for one scan as JSON or CSV (SRS Ch10 §4).

The renderer is read-only: it never mutates any database state and
never alters the canonical finding/severity/lifecycle values
established by the scan pipeline (Ch10 §3 integrity constraint).

get.description:
Direct single-entry lookup.

The previous implementation pulled the newest 200 entries and
searched them in Python, so a valid entry older than that window
was unreachable. ``AuditService.get_entry`` resolves by id and
applies the same v1 fail-closed visibility rule used by
``query_entries``.

TargetResponse.title: TargetResponse
TargetResponse.description:
Target representation incl. derived attestation status.

``status`` is always PENDING_ATTESTATION until the authorization
attestation feature lands (Chapter 5 Section 4/5): a target exists but is
unscannable until a CONFIRMED attestation is presented.
